decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core camera business that remained on its own product page through 2024, it is a low-cost strategic option to keep while market adoption in long-cycle space programs continues to unfold.
The product has direct evidence of mission use and launch success, so its value is no longer highly speculative and management would almost certainly retain it.
Although still somewhat uncertain, it builds on existing sensor capabilities and was maintained prominently on the website, making it worth keeping open in a growing and R&D-intensive space market.

Its lighter website presence suggests a more experimental offer, but miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR fits the firm's direction and the option value of waiting is still likely higher than immediate withdrawal.

As a newly launched radiation-hard camera closely aligned with the firm's heritage, it is too early to judge negatively and inexpensive to keep on the market while qualification and customer decisions mature.

This is a newer and more niche product with less visible market traction, but it still leverages established navigation and imaging know-how and is worth retaining as an exploratory option for future missions.
